# The ꜥAsherah file: from asherah to the temple it became
Every name in this series was once flattened to fit a keyboard. **ꜥAsherah** is what the evidence put back.

ꜥAsherah does not star in the great combat myths; she rules by relationship. Her appearances in the Baꜥal Cycle show a goddess who can approach the high god, sway his decisions, and guarantee the succession of kings. She is the still center around which the violent younger gods revolve. In KTU 1. 4, Baꜥal longs for a palace but cannot win Ēl's approval directly.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** ꜥAsherah
- **ASCII form:** asherah
- **Meaning:** "Canaanite mother goddess, consort of Ēl and patroness of childbirth"
- **Domain of influence:** Mother Goddess, Lady of the Sea
- **Pantheon:** Canaanite
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** 𐎀𐎘𐎗𐎚
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 36 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **Ἀσερά**. On the evidence, it means "Canaanite mother goddess, consort of Ēl and patroness of childbirth".

**ꜥAsherah** preserves its form without added diacritics: the restoration here is the exactness of the spelling itself, the form the tradition's own sources record. *asherah* and **ꜥAsherah** may look interchangeable to a search box; they are not interchangeable to a philologist.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **ꜥAsherah** lives at [/sites/asherah/](/sites/asherah/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/asherah/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/asherah/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/asherah/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **ꜥAsherah** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Wedding, Family & Maternity** — Patroness of childbirth; the mother who intercedes.
- **Women's Health & Femtech** — Patroness of childbirth; the ancient mother goddess.
- **Maritime, Shipping & Ocean Industries** — Lady of the Sea, patroness invoked by Levantine seafarers.

This is the part of the file that surprises people: a four-thousand-year-old name, mapping cleanly onto twenty-first-century trades. The patterns are not marketing — they are the same myths, read forward.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Canaanite tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Enūma Eliš](/texts/enuma-elish/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
## The File Continues

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/asherah/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.

Continue the series — previous file: **Ašavahišta** ([read it here](/sites/ashavahista/blog/restoration/)) · next file: **Aššur** ([read it here](/sites/ashur/blog/restoration/)).

*The Restoration Files are written from the same canonical record as the temples themselves: the lexicon, the lore catalog, the pattern atlas, and the cited scholarly sources. If a file ever disagrees with its temple, the temple is right — tell us, and the file will be corrected.*
